units.title: Component 1: Principles of Design and Technology

outcomes.text: Compare hardwoods (oak, mahogany, beech) and softwoods (pine, cedar) and choose the right wood for a use.
Compare ferrous metals, non-ferrous metals and alloys such as steel, aluminium, brass, and pick suitably.
Compare thermoplastics, thermosetting plastics and elastomers by properties and uses.
Compare composites such as carbon fibre, GRP, MDF and plywood and select appropriately.
Choose drawing papers, printing papers and boards for given purposes.
Compare natural and manmade fibres and textile treatments such as flame resistance and PTFE.
Describe smart materials such as shape memory alloys, thermochromic and photochromic materials, and where they are used.
Judge materials by conductivity, strength, elasticity, plasticity, malleability, ductility, hardness, toughness, durability and biodegradability.
Choose and safely use processes and tools: heat treatment, alloying, printing, casting, machining, moulding, lamination and marking out.
Use specialist measuring tools such as gauges, callipers, micrometers, jigs and go/no-go gauges to get required precision.
Communicate designs with isometric and perspective drawings, orthographic working drawings, nets and reports, translating between them.
Choose and safely use adhesives, mechanical fixings, heat joining and wood joints, knowing their pros and cons.
Choose finishes and preservation methods for materials, and paper and board finishing, to prevent degradation.
Set up and safely operate CAD, CAM, CNC machines and rapid prototyping, and weigh their advantages and disadvantages.

topics.title: 5 Factors influencing the development of products

outcomes.text: Explain how user-centred design (needs, purpose, functionality, innovation, authenticity) makes products fit for purpose.
Apply anthropometric data and ergonomic factors when designing products and environments.
Explain how aesthetics, ergonomics and anthropometrics shape design, including form over function and form follows function.
Describe key design movements and figures, from Arts and Crafts to Memphis, and their influence.
Discuss social, moral and ethical effects of mass production, high-technology manufacture and the global marketplace.

topics.title: 7 Safe working practices, potential hazards and risk assessment

outcomes.text: Work safely, recognise hazards and carry out and record risk assessments with control measures.
Describe one-off, batch and high-volume production.
Compare quality control, quality assurance and Total Quality Management (ISO 9000).
Explain modern manufacturing systems: scheduling, robotics, automated handling, flexible and lean production, JIT, QRM and data integration.

topics.title: 9 Designing for maintenance and the cleaner environment

subtopics.title: Cleaner design across the life cycle

outcomes.text: Reduce environmental impact across a product's life cycle: material choice, manufacture, distribution, use, repair and end of life.
Weigh cost to consumer and manufacturer against sustainability of cleaner technologies.
Explain the Consumer Rights Act 2015 and Sale of Goods Act 1979 for consumers and manufacturers.
Explain health and safety law (HSE, HSW Act 1974, PPE, signage, COSHH) and consequences of ignoring it.

topics.title: 11 Information handling, modelling and forward planning

outcomes.text: Gather and analyse marketing data, manage innovation and use feasibility studies to decide.
Model project costs with budgets and production planning, and select tools and processes.
Protect designs through patents, copyright, design rights and trademarks.
Explain how British, European and International standards (kite mark, CE, ISO) affect design and manufacture.
Use user-centred design, circular economy and systems thinking to explore, create and evaluate ideas.

subtopics.title: Project management and product life cycle

outcomes.text: Compare critical path analysis, scrum and Six Sigma as project management strategies.
Explain cost, sales and profit across the introduction, growth, maturity and decline stages of a product.
